newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan telecom still seen as good buy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan telecom still seen as good buy.

text.p: State-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd (PTCL) is still a good buy despite concerns about the impact on its earnings of a convertible bond issue and a global telecom deal, analysts said on Tuesday.
"We believe that the PTCL share is undervalued at the current price," said a research report of Jardine Fleming Pakistan, received by Reuters on Tuesday.
It said that on a conservative line growth assumption of 11.2 percent for 1996/97 (July-June) and 12 percent for 1997/98, the stock was trading at attractive multiples.
"Considering the attractive valuations and the revenue growth potential, we believe the stock has healthy upside from the current levels," it said.

PTCL fell 2.95 rupees to 30.40 rupees on Monday on profit-taking spurred by falling rates of its global depositary receipts (GDRs) abroad. It rose 1.25 rupees to 31.65 near midday on Tuesday on new accounts day buying.

Analyst Rizwan Butt of Khadim Ali Shah Bukhari & Co said the GDRs eased as investors sold them to raise cash to invest in this month's issue of $150 million worth of five-year bonds exchangeable into PTCL "A" shares held by the government.
He said the bond issue would have no surprise impact on PTCL's balance sheet. "The cost of the bond issue was already calculated in the projections for 1996/97 earnings," he said.

Jardine Fleming said bond-holders might not switch into PTCL shares immediately as a six percent coupon and a 7.5 percent conversion premium were attractive for those looking for a covered downside while enjoying the scrip's upside potential.
"We estimate that PTCL's common stock would need to double in price in the next three years for it to offer a return superior to the exchangeable bond," Jardine Fleming said.
The report said PTCL's price behaviour had been erratic with standard deviations of 18.9 percent.
"While bond-holders will be covered against adverse price behaviour, the stock volatility will add to the bond's value by increasing the price of the embedded call option," it added.

Analysts say the risk of a reduction in total accounting rates -- those at which PTCL's international call traffic are settled -- after a global telecom deal in Geneva was significant because much of its revenue was linked to international traffic.

Pakistan was among 68 countries that joined this month's Geneva deal to liberalise the $600 billion world telecom market, but was also among the five nations to secure exemptions from granting a uniform most-favoured-nation status to all countries.

Kalim Aziz, research head at ING Baring Securities, said the issue posed no immediate threat as the latest proposal before the World Trade Organisation was to bring accounting rates down by 75 percent in the next six to seven years.
Jardine Fleming said the U.S. decision to slash accounting rates with all big telecom companies was a cause for concern, but the United States might find it hard to implement quickly.
It said the government was likely to raise domestic telephone tariffs in fiscal 1997/98, which could add up to 20 percent to PTCL earnings for that year.
PTCL earned 19 billion rupees ($472.4 million) in the first half of 1995/96 for a net profit of 8.9 billion rupees. Analysts project whole-year earnings at 16.9 to 17 billion rupees.
